pr.title: feat: image cropping
pr.background: Excalidraw is a whiteboard editor. A scene is a list of elements, and an image element shows a picture stored under its `fileId`. The element's `x`, `y`, `width` and `height` describe a frame, and the picture is stretched to fill the frame. `App` keeps the editor state, `AppState`, and two canvases draw from it: the static canvas draws the elements through [`renderElement`](packages/excalidraw/renderer/renderElement.ts#L690), and the interactive canvas draws the selection border and the transform handles that resize an element. Undo and redo replay recorded changes of the elements and of a few watched state keys, and the SVG export writes each image as a `<symbol>` that holds an `<image>`. Actions are named commands that the properties panel, the context menu and the command palette share.
pr.problem: No linked issue: the PR description says image cropping has long been requested and was implemented before in excalidraw/excalidraw#6517 (a pull request at github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/6517), and restarts that work on a new branch. Today an image can only be resized, and a resize stretches the whole picture to the new frame, so showing part of a picture means editing it outside the editor. An image element has no field that says which part of its picture to show, the draw call [passes the whole picture to `drawImage`](packages/excalidraw/renderer/renderElement.ts#L366), the SVG export sets the `<image>` to 100% of its `<symbol>` whatever the element shows, and the editor has no mode where the handles trim an edge instead of resizing.
pr.solution: This PR adds cropping in seven parts, followed by a mechanical one. [An image element gets a `crop` rectangle that is `null` for the whole picture](crop-data), and resizing or flipping leaves it alone. [The canvas and the SVG export draw only the cropped region](crop-draw). [A double click, Enter, a panel button, the context menu or the command palette starts crop mode, and Escape, Enter or a click outside ends it](crop-session). [In crop mode the handles trim an edge](crop-handles), with a 10-unit minimum and Shift for the ratio, and [dragging inside the image slides the picture under the frame](crop-pan). [While cropping, the rest of the picture shows at 10% opacity](crop-preview). [Undo and redo restore the crop and the crop mode](crop-history). [The snapshots, a renamed border property and the SVG attribute order follow](renames).

cards.title: Image element type
cards.summary: The shapes of every scene element. [`ExcalidrawImageElement`](packages/excalidraw/element/types.ts#L144) is the element that shows a picture stored under its `fileId`.
bullets: New `ImageCrop` type and a `crop: ImageCrop | null` field on image elements.

changes.problem: Today [`ExcalidrawImageElement`](packages/excalidraw/element/types.ts#L144) holds `fileId`, `status` and `scale`, and its `width` and `height` always stretch the whole picture. Showing only a part of a picture would mean replacing the stored file, and the original would be lost.
changes.change: This PR adds [`ImageCrop`](packages/excalidraw/element/types.ts#L135), a rectangle `x`, `y`, `width`, `height` in the picture's own pixels plus the picture's `naturalWidth` and `naturalHeight`, and a [`crop: ImageCrop | null` field](packages/excalidraw/element/types.ts#L153) on image elements.

snippets.text: /** X and Y scale factors <-1, 1>, used for image axis flipping */

changes.result: `null` means the whole picture and a rectangle means that part of it, so every reader of an image element has one field to consult and the stored file stays whole. The PR description names the data `naturalDimension: [number, number]`; the code stores `naturalWidth` and `naturalHeight` instead.

reaches.effect: A resize or flip writes size or [`scale`](packages/excalidraw/element/resizeElements.ts#L963) through [`mutateElement`](packages/excalidraw/element/resizeElements.ts#L1005) and never `crop`, so the rectangle stays in picture pixels and is drawn into the new width and height. A flipped image keeps its `crop` and `scale` flips the drawing.

The stats panel's width and height fields call [`resizeElement`](packages/excalidraw/components/Stats/Dimension.tsx#L58) with the aspect ratio kept for images, so a cropped image is resized with its `crop` unchanged and the cropped region scales with the element.

unaffected.reason: They build images through [`newImageElement`](packages/excalidraw/element/newElement.ts#L491), which gives `null` when the caller passes no `crop`.
They read an image element's `status` and `fileId` to sync and load files, and never its size or `crop`, for example [the `status === "saved"` check](excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx#L354).

They name the image type in a guard or a union and read `x`, `y`, `width` and `height`, which already describe the cropped frame, for example [`isImageElement` tests `type`](packages/excalidraw/element/typeChecks.ts#L37-L40).

They decide by type and by pending status, not by the picture shown: [images are draggable from inside](packages/excalidraw/element/collision.ts#L41), and [a pending image is skipped](packages/excalidraw/scene/Renderer.ts#L83).
It asserts only [`scale`](packages/excalidraw/tests/flip.test.tsx#L750) after a flip, and `crop` is `null` for the images it builds.

cards.title: newElement.ts
cards.summary: Constructors for scene elements. [`newImageElement`](packages/excalidraw/element/newElement.ts#L474) builds an image element from options and defaults.
bullets: `newImageElement` takes an optional `crop` and defaults it to `null`.

changes.problem: Today [`newImageElement`](packages/excalidraw/element/newElement.ts#L474) returns an object with no `crop`. Once the type requires the field, every image built through it would lack a value that readers of `element.crop` expect.
changes.change: This PR adds [`crop` to the options](packages/excalidraw/element/newElement.ts#L480) and [returns `opts.crop ?? null`](packages/excalidraw/element/newElement.ts#L491).
changes.result: A new image has `crop: null` unless the caller passes one, so a freshly inserted image shows its whole picture and no reader sees `undefined`.

unaffected.reason: They use other constructors or helpers from the file, such as [`newTextElement`](packages/excalidraw/element/newElement.ts#L216) for bound text, and never build an image.
It re-exports [`newImageElement`](packages/excalidraw/element/index.ts#L15) unchanged, so callers import the same name.

cards.title: restore.ts
cards.summary: Normalises elements read from a file, local storage or a collaborator. [`restoreElement`](packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts#L199) rebuilds each element with defaults for fields an older file lacks.
bullets: A restored image gets `crop: element.crop ?? null`.

changes.problem: Today the [`image` case of `restoreElement`](packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts#L260) copies `status`, `fileId` and `scale`. A scene saved before this PR has no `crop`, so a restored image would carry `undefined` where the draw code expects a rectangle or `null`.
changes.change: This PR adds [`crop: element.crop ?? null`](packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts#L261) to that case.
changes.result: An old scene loads with `crop: null` and shows its whole pictures, and a scene saved with a crop keeps it. Without the line, an old image has no `crop` property, which is falsy in the draw code but is not the declared type.

unaffected.reason: They receive elements that `restoreElement` already normalised, and read `x`, `y`, `width` and `height`, not `crop`. [`restoreElements`](packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts#L446) is the entry they call.

cards.title: dragElements.ts

changes.problem: Today [`dragNewElement`](packages/excalidraw/element/dragElements.ts#L156) writes only position, size and text auto-resize. The size an image had when the user finished placing it is not kept anywhere.

cards.title: cropElement.ts
cards.summary: New module for cropping. [`cropElement`](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L31) turns a handle drag into the next frame and `crop` of an image, and [`getUncroppedImageElement`](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L475) describes the whole picture around the frame.
bullets: `cropElement` trims from a side or corner, keeps 10 units, holds a ratio with Shift and handles flipped images.
`recomputeOrigin` keeps the opposite corner fixed under rotation.
`getUncroppedImageElement` and `getUncroppedWidthAndHeight` give the whole picture's frame and size.

changes.problem: The editor has no code that turns a pointer position on a side or corner handle into a smaller frame and the matching rectangle of the picture. A plain resize would scale the whole picture, and a crop has to keep the picture's scale while moving one edge.
changes.change: This PR adds [`cropElement`](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L31). It reads the picture's uncropped size, rotates the pointer into the element's frame, and for each handle letter in the name moves that edge: [`nextHeight` or `nextWidth` is the pointer distance, clamped between `MINIMAL_CROP_SIZE` and the remaining picture](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L91). [`updateCropWidthAndHeight`](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L125) turns the frame size into picture pixels, and [`adjustFlipForHandle`](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L132) moves `crop.x` or `crop.y` for the edges that move the picture's origin, in reverse for a flipped axis.
changes.result: Dragging an edge changes the frame and the rectangle together, so the picture does not move or rescale, and a frame never gets smaller than 10 units or larger than the picture left on that side. "Cropping changes the dimension" and "Cropping has minimal sizes" check the size bounds.

changes.problem: With Shift held, the frame has to keep its width-to-height ratio while one edge or corner moves. A side handle moves one dimension, so the other has to follow and must stay inside the picture on both sides of the frame's centre. A corner handle follows whichever dimension the pointer moved more.
changes.change: When `widthAspectRatio` is passed, each case of [the `switch` on the handle](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L159) recomputes the other dimension from the ratio. [`n` and `s`](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L166) cap the width at twice the nearer picture edge and re-centre `crop.x`; [`w` and `e`](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L214) do the same with height and `crop.y`; each corner compares [`changeInWidth` with `changeInHeight`](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L258) to pick the dimension to follow.
changes.result: The ratio holds until a picture edge stops it, then the frame stops growing, which "Preserve aspect ratio" checks with a 50 by 50 square at the picture's corner that cannot expand. Without the caps the frame could extend past the picture and the rectangle would leave it.

changes.problem: After the frame size changes, the frame's `x` and `y` must change too, so the corner opposite the dragged handle stays where it was. The image may be rotated, and a rotation turns about the frame's centre, which moves when the size changes.
changes.change: This PR adds [`recomputeOrigin`](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L404). It takes the opposite corner of the starting frame, builds the new top-left from the new size, rotates it about the old and new centres by the element's angle, and [returns the origin shifted by the difference between the element and its resized bounds](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L468).

+  // adjust topLeft to new rotation point

changes.result: The edge or corner opposite the handle stays put on screen for a rotated image as well, so the image does not drift while it is trimmed.

changes.problem: Once the user drags every edge back out, `crop` would hold a rectangle that equals the whole picture. A non-null `crop` takes the crop branches in every reader, though it shows the same thing as `null`.
changes.change: This PR sets [`crop = null` when its width and height are close to the natural size](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L389-L392), using `isCloseTo`, and returns that with the new frame.

snippets.text: +  // reset crop to null if we're back to orig size

changes.result: An image trimmed back to the full picture is stored as uncropped. The test file checks only that sizes change and stay within bounds, not this reset.

changes.problem: Today an image's size is its drawn size. Once `crop` is set, `width` and `height` describe only the visible part, and [the SVG export](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts#L426) needs the size of the whole picture at the same scale to place it inside the visible window.
changes.change: This PR adds [`getUncroppedWidthAndHeight`](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L546), which divides `width` by the share of the picture's width that `crop.width` covers, and `height` the same way, and returns the element's own size when `crop` is `null`.
changes.result: A caller gets the width and height the whole picture would have at the cropped image's scale. An image with no `crop` returns its own size, so the SVG export can call it for every image.

changes.problem: To show the whole picture faintly behind the frame, the renderer needs an element that covers the full picture at the right place and angle. The cropped element's `x` and `y` are the frame's, so they are not the picture's origin.
changes.change: This PR adds [`getUncroppedImageElement`](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L475). For a cropped image it finds the frame's top-left and edge directions with the angle applied, [moves back along them by the cropped-away `cropX` and `cropY`](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L509), rotates the result back, and returns a copy with the uncropped size and `crop: null`. [`adjustCropPosition`](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L565) mirrors the offsets for a flipped axis, and an uncropped image is returned as it is.
changes.result: Drawing that element with the ordinary image draw shows the whole picture exactly behind the frame, at the same angle and flip. No test in the PR checks the position.

cards.title: actionCropEditor.tsx
cards.summary: New action module. [`actionToggleCropEditor`](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionCropEditor.tsx#L9) is the named action that starts cropping and shows the panel button.
bullets: `perform` sets `croppingElementId` to the selected image.
`predicate` is true only for one selected image while no crop is in progress.
`PanelComponent` is an icon button that runs the action.

changes.problem: The panel, the context menu and the command palette all work through registered actions, and no action starts cropping. A user who does not know the double click or Enter has no visible way in.
changes.change: This PR adds the action `cropEditor`. [`perform`](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionCropEditor.tsx#L16) sets `croppingElementId` to the selected image with `isCropping` false and captures an undo step. [`predicate`](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionCropEditor.tsx#L31) is true for exactly one selected image when `croppingElementId` is empty. [`PanelComponent`](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionCropEditor.tsx#L42) renders a `ToolButton` with the crop icon that calls `updateData(null)`. The `keywords` `image` and `crop` make the palette find it.

cards.title: appState.ts
cards.summary: Defaults and storage rules for the editor state. [`getDefaultAppState`](packages/excalidraw/appState.ts#L20) builds a new state, and [`APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF`](packages/excalidraw/appState.ts#L129) says which keys go to the browser, an export or the server.
bullets: Defaults: `isCropping: false`, `croppingElementId: null`.
Neither key is saved anywhere.

changes.problem: `AppState` gets two fields, and a new editor has no values for them. Code that reads `state.croppingElementId` would see `undefined` and, in a test snapshot, a missing key.
changes.change: This PR adds [`isCropping: false` and `croppingElementId: null`](packages/excalidraw/appState.ts#L119) to the default state.

changes.change: This PR adds [rows for both keys with `browser`, `export` and `server` set to false](packages/excalidraw/appState.ts#L242-L243).

userToFollow: { browser: false, export: false, server: false },

cards.summary: Shared types of the editor. [`AppState`](packages/excalidraw/types.ts#L230) is the editor's state, and the canvas state types pick the keys each canvas needs.
bullets: `AppState` gets `isCropping` and `croppingElementId`.
The interactive and static canvas states and the observed state list the keys they use.

changes.problem: The editor state has no field that says an image is in crop mode or which image.
changes.change: This PR adds [`isCropping: boolean` and a nullable `croppingElementId`](packages/excalidraw/types.ts#L397-L398) to `AppState`.

snippets.text: /** the socket ids of the users following the current user */

changes.problem: The shortcuts dialog does not list the ways to start and stop cropping.
changes.change: This PR adds [a row for starting a crop](packages/excalidraw/components/HelpDialog.tsx#L226) with a double click or Enter, and [a row for finishing](packages/excalidraw/components/HelpDialog.tsx#L231) with Enter or Escape.

bullets: Crop mode and a selected image each get a hint.

changes.problem: The hint line has no hint for an image, so a user does not learn that a double click or Enter crops it, or how to leave crop mode.
changes.change: This PR adds, ahead of the selection-tool hints, [a hint for crop mode](packages/excalidraw/components/HintViewer.tsx#L104) when `croppingElementId` is set, and [a hint for one selected image](packages/excalidraw/components/HintViewer.tsx#L108).
changes.result: Selecting one image shows "Double click the image or press ENTER to crop the image", and opening the editor shows how to finish.

cards.title: icons.tsx
cards.summary: The editor's icon components, such as [`upIcon`](packages/excalidraw/components/icons.tsx#L2143).

cards.title: InteractiveCanvas.tsx
cards.summary: The canvas for selection, handles and cursors. [`InteractiveCanvas`](packages/excalidraw/components/canvases/InteractiveCanvas.tsx#L65) is memoised on a picked subset of the state.
bullets: `isCropping` and `croppingElementId` join the picked state.

changes.problem: The canvas is wrapped in [`React.memo` with `areEqual`](packages/excalidraw/components/canvases/InteractiveCanvas.tsx#L239), which compares only the keys that [`getRelevantAppStateProps`](packages/excalidraw/components/canvases/InteractiveCanvas.tsx#L176) picks. A change to a key outside that list does not redraw the canvas.
changes.change: This PR adds [`isCropping` and `croppingElementId`](packages/excalidraw/components/canvases/InteractiveCanvas.tsx#L206) to the picked keys.
changes.result: Entering or leaving crop mode, and starting or ending a handle drag, redraw the interactive canvas, which swaps the transform handles for the crop handles. Without the keys the canvas would keep showing the old handles until some other picked key changed.

unaffected.reason: None of the four reads `isCropping` or `croppingElementId`; they hold constants, render-config types, the visible-element filter and resize code.

cards.title: StaticCanvas.tsx
cards.summary: The canvas that draws the elements. [`StaticCanvas`](packages/excalidraw/components/canvases/StaticCanvas.tsx#L29) is memoised on a picked subset of the state.
bullets: `croppingElementId` joins the picked state.

changes.problem: The element canvas redraws only when [`areEqual`](packages/excalidraw/components/canvases/StaticCanvas.tsx#L113) finds a changed picked key, a changed scene or a changed visible list. Entering crop mode changes only `croppingElementId`, so the faint preview would not appear or disappear.
changes.change: This PR adds [`croppingElementId`](packages/excalidraw/components/canvases/StaticCanvas.tsx#L110) to the picked keys.
changes.result: Starting and ending crop mode redraw the elements, so the preview shows and hides at once.

unaffected.reason: They host, feed or mutate the canvas and none reads `croppingElementId`; the canvas only compares the picked keys.

cards.title: store.ts
cards.summary: Captures changes for undo and redo. [`getObservedAppState`](packages/excalidraw/store.ts#L15) picks the state keys that history watches.
bullets: `croppingElementId` is observed.

changes.problem: History records a change of the keys [`getObservedAppState`](packages/excalidraw/store.ts#L15) returns. `croppingElementId` is not among them, so entering or leaving crop mode never appears in a recorded change.
changes.change: This PR adds [`croppingElementId`](packages/excalidraw/store.ts#L24) to the observed state.
changes.result: A step that enters or leaves crop mode carries the id, so undo and redo can restore the mode with the crop.

cards.title: change.ts
cards.summary: Deltas for undo and redo. [`AppStateChange`](packages/excalidraw/change.ts#L416) and [`ElementsChange`](packages/excalidraw/change.ts#L807) apply a recorded difference to the state and the elements.
bullets: A delta may carry `croppingElementId`; one pointing at a deleted element is reset.
An element delta applies `crop` as it was recorded.

changes.problem: Undo and redo apply a recorded state difference, and [`filterInvisibleChanges`](packages/excalidraw/change.ts#L644) drops the keys of a difference that would change nothing the user can see. An unknown `croppingElementId` key would be applied as it is, and if the image was deleted since, crop mode would point at an element that is not there.
changes.change: This PR adds [a `croppingElementId` case](packages/excalidraw/change.ts#L632). It looks the id up in the next elements, marks the difference visible when the element exists and is not deleted, and otherwise sets the key to `null`. [`stripElementsProps`](packages/excalidraw/change.ts#L774) lists the key with the other element-dependent ones, so it is kept apart from standalone keys such as `name`.
changes.result: Undo or redo returns to crop mode on a live image, and never to crop mode on a deleted one.

changes.problem: Today [`applyDelta`](packages/excalidraw/change.ts#L1208) writes the delta's `inserted` partial through [`newElementWith`](packages/excalidraw/change.ts#L1264), which leaves out a key whose value is `undefined`. For an image, a delta whose `deleted` side holds a `crop` and whose `inserted` side has none would leave the element's current crop in place instead of clearing it.
changes.change: This PR adds, for an image, [a `crop` override](packages/excalidraw/change.ts#L1238-L1246). When `deleted.crop` or `inserted.crop` is set, it writes `inserted.crop ?? null` as the element's `crop`, and otherwise leaves `crop` alone. [`ElementPartial`](packages/excalidraw/change.ts#L798-L801) becomes generic so the image delta is typed.

snippets.text: +      // we want to override `crop` only if modified so that we don't reset

changes.result: Undoing a trim writes the earlier rectangle back, and undoing the first trim writes `null`, so the whole picture shows again. An undo or redo of a delta with no `crop` on either side leaves the crop as it is, which the code comment gives as the reason for the condition. The PR has no test for undoing a crop.

cards.title: renderElement.ts
cards.summary: Draws elements on a canvas. [`drawElementOnCanvas`](packages/excalidraw/renderer/renderElement.ts#L377) paints one element, and [`renderElement`](packages/excalidraw/renderer/renderElement.ts#L690) chooses between drawing directly for export and drawing from a cached canvas.
bullets: An image is drawn from its `crop` rectangle.
Every element drawn on screen gets a fresh canvas each render.
In crop mode the whole picture is drawn at 10% opacity first.

changes.problem: Today the image case of [`drawElementOnCanvas`](packages/excalidraw/renderer/renderElement.ts#L366) passes the whole picture to `drawImage`, so a `crop` rectangle would be ignored and the cropped element would show the full picture squeezed into the smaller frame.
changes.change: This PR picks [the rectangle to draw](packages/excalidraw/renderer/renderElement.ts#L440-L448), which is `element.crop` or the whole natural size, and passes it as the source rectangle of `drawImage`, with the element's width and height as the target.

snippets.text: +        const { x, y, width, height } = element.crop

changes.result: The canvas shows only the part of the picture inside the rectangle, scaled into the frame. An image with `crop` null draws as before.

changes.problem: Today an element drawn on screen is [generated once and cached](packages/excalidraw/renderer/renderElement.ts#L524), and the cache is rebuilt only for zoom, theme, bound-text version, frame opacity and arrow labels. [`mutateElement`](packages/excalidraw/element/mutateElement.ts#L92) clears the cache only when `width`, `height`, `fileId` or `points` change. A change to `crop` alone, such as sliding the picture, would keep showing the old cached canvas.
changes.change: This PR calls [`generateElementCanvas` for the element on every render](packages/excalidraw/renderer/renderElement.ts#L969) and draws that canvas with `drawElementFromCanvas`, in place of drawing the cached one. The call is not limited to images.
changes.result: A crop-only change shows on the next render. Every element that takes this path rebuilds its offscreen canvas on each render instead of drawing the cached canvas, which the code still builds through `generateElementWithCanvas`.

changes.problem: While trimming or sliding, the user sees only the cropped part. The picture outside the frame is not drawn, so they cannot see what a handle will reveal or where the picture ends.
changes.change: This PR adds, ahead of the normal draw, [a block for the element whose id is `croppingElementId` and whose `crop` is not null](packages/excalidraw/renderer/renderElement.ts#L941-L944). It sets `globalAlpha` to `0.1`, builds a canvas for [`getUncroppedImageElement`](packages/excalidraw/renderer/renderElement.ts#L949), draws it and restores the context.
changes.result: The whole picture shows faintly, with the cropped part drawn at full opacity over it. Outside crop mode, and for an uncropped image, the block is skipped.

reaches.effect: `exportToCanvas` calls [`renderStaticScene`](packages/excalidraw/scene/export.ts#L222), which draws each element through `renderElement`, so a PNG or canvas export draws a cropped image by its `crop`.

unaffected.reason: It still drops the cached canvas whenever it drops a shape: [`ShapeCache.delete`](packages/excalidraw/scene/ShapeCache.ts#L68) calls `delete` on the [`elementWithCanvasCache`](packages/excalidraw/renderer/renderElement.ts#L519) that `generateElementWithCanvas` still fills, so a cleared shape is still rebuilt.
The word `crop` in them is the middle of `microphone`, in the call-status icon names, and they draw no image.
Its `crop` is the clipping of an export to a frame, for example "exporting frame should include overlapping elements, but crop to frame", and its scenes hold no image element.

cards.title: staticSvgScene.ts
cards.summary: Writes the scene as SVG. [`renderElementToSvg`](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts#L79) turns one element into SVG nodes.
bullets: A cropped image becomes a symbol with a `viewBox` on the visible window.

changes.problem: Today [the image `<symbol>`](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts#L417) holds an `<image>` that is 100% wide and tall, so a cropped element would export its whole picture squeezed into the frame.
changes.change: This PR sets [the `<image>` to the uncropped width and height](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts#L436) and the symbol's [`viewBox` to the crop's origin in that size and the element's `width` and `height`](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts#L428-L436) when `element.crop` is set. The 100% attributes stay for an uncropped image.
changes.result: The SVG shows only the visible window of the picture at the cropped size. [The symbol id comes from the file and the symbol is built only when none has that id](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts#L416), so two images of one file share the attributes of the first one exported.

changes.problem: The `<image>` attributes are set in the order width, height, href, preserveAspectRatio, and an SVG snapshot records the attributes in the order they were set.
changes.change: This PR moves the [`100%` width and height](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts#L439) from before `href` to the `else` branch after `preserveAspectRatio`, so the attributes are set in a new order.
changes.result: The exported `<image>` of an uncropped picture has the same four attributes with the same values; only their order in the string differs, which is what the `export.test.tsx` snapshot records.

reaches.effect: `exportToSvg` calls [`renderSceneToSvg`](packages/excalidraw/scene/export.ts#L397), so an SVG export of a cropped image carries the `viewBox`.

cards.title: interactiveScene.ts
cards.summary: Draws selection chrome. [`_renderInteractiveScene`](packages/excalidraw/renderer/interactiveScene.ts#L729) paints selection borders, transform handles and other overlays on the interactive canvas.
bullets: Crop handles replace transform handles in crop mode.
An image's selection border has no padding.
`elementX1` to `elementY2` are renamed `x1` to `y2`.

changes.problem: In crop mode the image shows the ordinary selection box, corner squares and a rotation handle, which suggest a resize. The user needs marks at the corners of the frame that say which edge is trimmed.
changes.change: This PR adds [`renderCropHandles`](packages/excalidraw/renderer/interactiveScene.ts#L602), which strokes an L-shaped bracket at each corner of the image, rotated with it and sized by the zoom, and calls it when [`croppingElementId` is set and `isCropping` is not](packages/excalidraw/renderer/interactiveScene.ts#L1022). It also skips [the transform handles](packages/excalidraw/renderer/interactiveScene.ts#L1011) in crop mode and [the selection rectangle](packages/excalidraw/renderer/interactiveScene.ts#L784) during a trim.

snippets.text: +    const [[x, y], [x1s, y1s], [x1t, y1t], [x2s, y2s], [x2t, y2t]] = handle;
// do not show transform handles when text is being edited
+        // do not show transform handles when image is being cropped

changes.result: The user sees four corner brackets and no resize handles while the editor is open. During a drag the brackets are hidden, since the dragged edge itself is the cue.

changes.problem: Today a selected element's border is drawn [`DEFAULT_TRANSFORM_HANDLE_SPACING * 2` outside its frame](packages/excalidraw/renderer/interactiveScene.ts#L230). For a cropped image that is a gap between the border and the picture's edge, which is where the trim handles sit.
changes.change: This PR adds [`ElementSelectionBorder`](packages/excalidraw/renderer/interactiveScene.ts#L312) with an optional `padding`, reads [`elementProperties.padding ?? DEFAULT_TRANSFORM_HANDLE_SPACING * 2`](packages/excalidraw/renderer/interactiveScene.ts#L347), and passes [`0` for an image and for the element being cropped](packages/excalidraw/renderer/interactiveScene.ts#L954-L957).
changes.result: The border of any selected image hugs its frame, not only in crop mode. Other elements keep the padding.

changes.problem: The selection-border properties are named `elementX1`, `elementY1`, `elementX2` and `elementY2`.
changes.change: This PR renames them to [`x1`, `y1`, `x2` and `y2`](packages/excalidraw/renderer/interactiveScene.ts#L369) in the border function, the group selection and the multi-element highlight.
changes.result: The border is drawn at the same coordinates as before.

cards.title: transformHandles.ts
cards.summary: Positions of the resize and rotate handles. [`getTransformHandles`](packages/excalidraw/element/transformHandles.ts#L265) returns the handle boxes of an element.
bullets: An image's handles sit on its edge with no outward offset.

changes.problem: Today every handle is offset [`DEFAULT_TRANSFORM_HANDLE_SPACING` outside the frame](packages/excalidraw/element/transformHandles.ts#L145) and its dashed line has a margin. For crop, the handle has to sit on the picture's edge, since the trim follows the pointer to that edge.
changes.change: This PR adds [a `spacing` parameter](packages/excalidraw/element/transformHandles.ts#L133) to `getTransformHandlesFromCoords` that replaces the constant in the centring offset, and [`getTransformHandles` passes `0` as the margin and as the spacing for an image](packages/excalidraw/element/transformHandles.ts#L317).
changes.result: An image's handle boxes are centred on its frame, in crop mode and in ordinary resizing. Other elements get the same margin and spacing as before, since `undefined` selects the default.

unaffected.reason: They call or re-export [`getTransformHandles`](packages/excalidraw/element/transformHandles.ts#L265) for non-image elements, whose margin and spacing are unchanged.

`resizeElements.ts` takes the handle type that the hit test returns and does not compute positions. The image tests in `resize.test.tsx` find a handle through [`getTransformHandles`](packages/excalidraw/tests/helpers/ui.ts#L333) and press at its centre, so they follow the moved box.

cards.title: resizeTest.ts
cards.summary: Hit tests for the transform handles. [`resizeTest`](packages/excalidraw/element/resizeTest.ts#L42) returns the handle under a point.
bullets: An image's side-handle zone starts at its edge.

changes.problem: Today the side handles are tested on lines [`SIDE_RESIZING_THRESHOLD / zoom.value` outside the frame](packages/excalidraw/element/resizeTest.ts#L93), within that distance. An image's handles now sit on its edge, so a point outside the frame by that distance must no longer start a trim.
changes.change: This PR makes [`SPACING` zero for an image](packages/excalidraw/element/resizeTest.ts#L94) and keeps the hit distance in [`ZOOMED_SIDE_RESIZING_THRESHOLD`](packages/excalidraw/element/resizeTest.ts#L96), which `pointOnLineSegment` now uses.

snippets.text: // do not resize from the sides for linear elements with only two points

changes.result: The side zone of an image is the strip centred on its edge, as wide as before. For other elements `SPACING` and the hit distance are the same value as before.

unaffected.reason: The image resize tests press at the centre of a handle taken from [`getTransformHandles`](packages/excalidraw/tests/helpers/ui.ts#L333), which is inside the new zone, and `resizeElements.ts` receives the handle type it returns.

cards.title: cropElement.test.tsx
cards.summary: New test file. It renders the editor with one [200 by 100 image](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L37) selected before each test, and its tests drive crop mode through the mouse, the keyboard, [`UI.crop`](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L113) and the flip, export and duplicate helpers.
bullets: Four tests for entering and leaving crop mode.
Three tests for trimming sizes and the aspect ratio.
Duplicate, resize, flip and export tests.

changes.problem: Crop mode has four ways in and out that the editor offers by pointer and keyboard. The behaviour pinned here: the editor enters crop mode from a double click or Enter, and leaves it from a click outside the image or Escape, with `croppingElementId` naming the image while it lasts.
changes.change: This PR adds [`Enter and leave the crop editor`](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L67). Each test starts with `croppingElementId` null where it asserts that, then calls [`mouse.doubleClickOn(image)`](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L71) or [presses Enter](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L79) and reads the id, or starts in crop mode and [clicks 20 units outside the image](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L89) or [presses Escape](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L98).

+  it("enter the editor by pressing enter", () => {
+  it("leave the editor by pressing escape", () => {

changes.result: A change that stops the double click, Enter, the outside click or Escape from toggling `croppingElementId` fails one of the four. The tests do not open crop mode from the panel button, the context menu or the command palette.

changes.problem: Dragging a crop handle has to shrink the visible frame, keep it positive and at most as large as the picture, and keep the ratio under Shift. The behaviour pinned here is those bounds on the image's `width` and `height`.
changes.change: This PR adds [`Crop an image`](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L103). [`Cropping changes the dimension`](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L104) drags `w` and `n` by half the size and expects both sizes to shrink. [`Cropping has minimal sizes`](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L120) drags `w` and `n` by the whole size and expects both sizes to stay greater than 0. [`Preserve aspect ratio`](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L137) crops with the ratio kept, expects `width / height` to stay the same until a picture edge stops it, and checks a square at the picture's corner (the final steps expect `width` to equal `height`).

snippets.text: +    // test corner handle aspect ratio preserving

changes.result: A clamp that lets the frame reach zero or grow past the picture, or a ratio branch that drifts, fails these. Each test uses a random natural size and so does not pin a fixed crop rectangle.

changes.problem: Resizing or flipping an image after it is cropped must leave `crop` as it was, since `crop` is in picture pixels and the drawing scales it into the new frame. The behaviour pinned here is that `crop` stays the same object and the same numbers.
changes.change: This PR adds [`Resizing should not affect crop`](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L244), which crops, then resizes through `UI.resize` and expects `image.crop` to be the same object and equal to a clone taken before. [`Flipping does not change crop`](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L273) does the same for `actionFlipHorizontal` and `actionFlipVertical`. [`compareCrops`](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L58) compares each number with `toBeCloseTo`.

snippets.text: +  it("Resizing should not affect crop", async () => {

changes.result: Code that rewrites `crop` during a resize or a flip fails these two tests. The tests resize and flip the element through test helpers, not through the pointer path in `App`.

changes.problem: A duplicated image is a separate element, so cropping the copy must not change the original, and cropping the original must not change the copy. The behaviour pinned here is that the two elements keep their own sizes.
changes.change: This PR adds [`Cropping works independently of duplication`](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L202). It crops the image, copies it with [`duplicateElement`](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L215), crops each one in turn and expects only the cropped one's `width` and `height` to change.

snippets.text: +    const duplicatedImage = duplicateElement(null, new Map(), image, {});

changes.result: A duplicate that shares state with its source fails this test. It compares sizes and does not compare the `crop` objects.

changes.problem: An export of a cropped image has to keep the cropped frame. The behaviour pinned here is the exported shape: the width-to-height ratio of a PNG canvas and of the SVG equals that of the cropped element.
changes.change: This PR adds [`Exports should preserve crops`](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L300). It crops the image, calls [`exportToCanvas`](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L317) and [`exportToSvg`](packages/excalidraw/tests/cropElement.test.tsx#L327) with no padding, and expects each ratio `toBeCloseTo` the element's.
changes.result: An export that uses the whole picture's size instead of the frame fails this test. It reads only the outer `width` and `height`, so it does not check the `<symbol>` `viewBox` or which part of the picture is drawn.

cards.title: tests/helpers/ui.ts
cards.summary: Helpers that drive the editor in tests. [`UI`](packages/excalidraw/tests/helpers/ui.ts#L413) has static methods such as [`resize`](packages/excalidraw/tests/helpers/ui.ts#L557) that press a transform handle and move the pointer.
bullets: New `UI.crop` calls `cropElement` and updates the element.

changes.problem: A test that crops has to move a crop handle by a distance. Pressing the handle with the mouse would go through [`maybeHandleCrop` in `App`](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L10138), which only crops when [the picture is in the image cache](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L10170), and the test environment has no loaded picture (inferred: the PR gives no reason for calling `cropElement` directly).
changes.change: This PR adds [`UI.crop`](packages/excalidraw/tests/helpers/ui.ts#L566). It finds the handle's centre with [`getTransformHandles`](packages/excalidraw/tests/helpers/ui.ts#L574), adds the mouse move, calls [`cropElement`](packages/excalidraw/tests/helpers/ui.ts#L585) directly with the given natural size, and applies the result with [`API.updateElement`](packages/excalidraw/tests/helpers/ui.ts#L595).
changes.result: Tests can trim an image by a pointer distance with a chosen natural size. They skip the pointer path through `App`, so the image-cache guard in `maybeHandleCrop` and the pointer handlers are not covered by them.

cards.title: setupTests.ts
cards.summary: Vitest setup. It wraps [`console.error`](setupTests.ts#L102) to tag React `act()` warnings with the running test's name.
bullets: `args[0]?.includes(...)` becomes `args[0]?.includes?.(...)`.

changes.problem: The wrapper calls [`args[0]?.includes("act(")`](setupTests.ts#L107) on whatever `console.error` receives first. The optional chain protects `undefined`, and a first argument that is not a string, such as an object, has no `includes` and would throw inside the wrapper.
changes.change: This PR changes [the call to `includes` on the first argument to an optional call](setupTests.ts#L107), so a first argument without an `includes` method skips the check. The PR states no motive, so this one is inferred from the call. The change sits in this intent as the nearest match, since the crop tests are the only new tests in the PR.

snippets.text: // the react's act() warning usually doesn't contain any useful stack trace
// so we're catching the log and re-logging the message with the test name,
// also stripping the actual component stack trace as it's not useful

changes.result: A `console.error` call with a non-string first argument is passed on as before and no longer throws from the wrapper. Strings that contain `act(` are still re-logged with the test name.

bullets: Two new `appState` keys at their defaults.
A `cropEditor` context-menu entry.

changes.problem: The context-menu test records every item that [the view-mode menu](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L10397) and the element menu return, and the menu now includes the crop action.
changes.change: This PR adds a [`cropEditor` entry](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionCropEditor.tsx#L10) between two separators in the context-menu snapshot, with the label `helpDialog.cropStart`, the keywords `image` and `crop` and `viewMode: true`.

intents.title: Let an image element hold a crop of its picture
intents.outcome: After this PR, an image element has a `crop` that is either `null` or the rectangle of its picture that it shows, new and restored images start with `null`, and resizing or flipping an image leaves the crop as it was.

intents.title: Draw and export a cropped image as only its crop region
intents.outcome: After this PR, a cropped image is drawn on the canvas and written into an SVG export as only the part of the picture inside its `crop`, and an export keeps the cropped size.

builds_on.label: Reads the crop
builds_on.how: the draw call and the SVG export read [`element.crop`](packages/excalidraw/renderer/renderElement.ts#L440), the field `crop-data` adds.

intents.title: Let a user enter and leave an image's crop mode
intents.outcome: After this PR, a user starts cropping the one selected image with a double click, Enter, a panel button, the context menu or the command palette, and ends it with Escape, Enter or a click outside the image, with `appState.croppingElementId` naming the image for as long as it lasts.

intents.title: Let a user trim an image by dragging its handles
intents.outcome: After this PR, while an image is in crop mode, dragging a side or corner handle trims the image to the dragged edge, keeps at least 10 scene units, holds the aspect ratio with Shift, and does not resize the image.

builds_on.label: Needs crop mode
builds_on.how: [`maybeHandleCrop` returns early unless `croppingElementId` is set](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L10142-L10144), which `crop-session` sets.

builds_on.label: Writes the crop
builds_on.how: [`cropElement` returns the new `crop`](packages/excalidraw/element/cropElement.ts#L398-L400) that `crop-data` lets an element hold.

intents.title: Let a user slide the picture under the crop frame
